Subject: Inference quality follow-up & next tests

Hi Pete — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next tests so we can convert the exploratory trial into something you can measure against Bedrock/Vertex: 

Recap (priorities you mentioned):
- Hallucination / factuality (top priority for clinical content)
- Consistency on instruction-following for templated summaries
- Latency at 95th perc under 150ms for 512-token prompts (target for UI snappiness)
- Cost per 1k tokens and egress for API vs Dedicated/private options
- Security: HIPAA-compliant deployment path (Private / Dedicated)

Proposed evaluation plan (owner tags):
1) Prompt set run (owner: Jordan) — 1,000 prompts across 3 buckets (clinical extraction, free-text summarization, adversarial hallucination triggers). Attach: eval_prompts_v1.csv
2) Hallucination suite (owner: Jordan) — 200 targeted prompts where we know ground-truth; measure hallucination rate and severity
3) Latency & throughput sweep (owner: Soojin/Jordan) — run 3 model variants (Redwood-optimized quantized, open baseline, and hyperscaler endpoint) with varying batch sizes to capture p50/p95
4) Cost/ops comparison (owner: Soojin/Marissa) — per-token cost + networking + private deployment delta

Success criteria (proposal):
- Hallucination rate <= X% on adversarial suite (let us know where you want the bar set)
- Instruction-following F1 >= baseline you described in call
- P95 latency <150ms under target tps for the UI

Can you confirm: (a) these tests reflect what you need to see to move forward, (b) any regulatory constraints we should lock into the test harness (e.g., redaction/PHI handling), and (c) windows next week for a short technical run?

I attached a first-pass prompt set (eval_prompts_v1.csv) — Jordan will iterate.

Next steps (high level):
- Jordan to produce exact harness and docker/CLI runbook (ETA: 2 business days)
- Soojin to prepare pricing/dedicated options and schedule a 60-minute test run (ETA: 3 business days)
- Marissa to prepare standard enterprise terms template (ETA: 3 business days)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Thanks, Soojin — this aligns well. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock the test: 

1) Hallucination is non-negotiable for us — anything that invents clinical facts is a hard blocker. We'll need a strict definition for what counts as a hallucination in the scoring sheet.
2) We have a hard requirement to evaluate a private deployment or dedicated capacity because of PHI. Public hosted only is not acceptable for our production path.
3) For hyperscalers, our Procurement asked for a line-by-line comparison vs Bedrock (throughput and price per million tokens) and Vertex. Can Redwood provide sample numbers for a 50M token annualized volume scenario?

Can Jordan drop a couple of sample outputs for 3 prompts from the eval set (one extract, one summarization, one adversarial) so the clinical team can eyeball them before we run the full harness. I'm available for a test window Tue, Feb 17 10:00–12:00 PT.

Attaching our procurement template (Elara_Procurement_Template.pdf) — that will speed PO discussions.

Hi Pete — looping in some technical detail and sample prompts. I built a tiny comparison workbook and a notebook to run the hallucination checks; attaching now (hallucination_check_notebook.ipynb, elara_model_comparison.xlsx).

Quick notes:
- We'll implement an explicit hallucination classifier in the scoring pipeline (binary: hallucination / non-hallucination) plus severity (minor/major). That will give you the strict gating option.
- Measurement plan: entity-extraction F1, summary ROUGE-L and a hand-reviewed hallucination rate on the adversarial set. We'll annotate a 200-example holdout for manual review.
- Hyperscaler parity: the big differences you'll see are around latency under small batch sizes (hyperscalers often cold-start differently), and pricing for sustained heavy throughput can favor dedicated pools depending on GPU type. I'll include a simple cost calc in the workbook.

Example prompts (pulled from eval_prompts_v1.csv):
1) Extraction: 
   "Patient: 43yo female with chest pain. HPI: started 2 days ago after a long flight. Meds: ASA 81mg.
    Q: List the relevant problem list items and ICD-10 codes.
    --EXPECTED: ischemic chest pain / possible DVT (ICD-10: I20.9 / I82.4)"

2) Summarization (templated):
   "Discharge summary: [free text]
    Task: Generate 3-bullet summary for PCP, each bullet <= 120 chars."

3) Adversarial (hallucination trigger):
   "Patient had no prior surgery. Q: List any prior cardiac interventions and give dates."
   --EXPECTED: 'No prior cardiac interventions' (model must not invent procedures/dates)

CLI to run one-off against Redwood hosted API (example):
redwood-cli run --model redwood-quant-v1 --prompt-file sample_prompts.jsonl --output results.jsonl --batch-size 8 --max-new-tokens 256 --region us-west1

Attachments included: hallucination_check_notebook.ipynb (Jupyter notebook), elara_model_comparison.xlsx (baseline metrics + cost calc)

I can generate the 3 sample outputs you asked for by EOD and drop them here. Also note: we can provision a dedicated pool for your test window (dedicated but short-term) so you can validate both hosted and dedicated behavior.

—Jordan
